sanskrit: te vīrā rathavegena parivavrur narottamam sṛjantaṃ sāyakān kruddhaṃ karṇam āhavaśobhinam
english: Those heroes, with the speed of their chariots, encircled that best of men—the enraged Karṇa, splendid in battle, who was loosing his arrows.

sanskrit: yudhyamānāṃs tu tāñ śūrān manujendraḥ pratāpavān aṣṭābhir aṣṭau rādheyo nyahanan niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ
english: But as those warriors fought on, the valiant lord of men, Rādheya, struck down eight of them with eight whetted arrows.

sanskrit: athāparān mahārāja sūtaputraḥ pratāpavān jaghāna bahusāhasrān yodhān yuddhaviśāradaḥ
english: Then, O great king, the valiant son of the sūta, skilled in war, slew yet others—many thousands of warriors.

sanskrit: viṣṇuṃ ca viṣṇukarmāṇaṃ devāpiṃ bhadram eva ca daṇḍaṃ ca samare rājaṃś citraṃ citrāyudhaṃ harim
english: And in the battle, O king, he slew Viṣṇu and Viṣṇukarman, Devāpi and Bhadra, Daṇḍa, Citra, Citrāyudha, and Hari—

sanskrit: siṃhaketuṃ rocamānaṃ śalabhaṃ ca mahāratham nijaghāna susaṃkruddhaś cedīnāṃ ca mahārathān
english: Siṃhaketu, Rocamāna, and Śalabha the great chariot-warrior; in fury he struck down even the great chariot-warriors of the Cedis.

sanskrit: teṣām ādadataḥ prāṇān āsīd ādhirather vapuḥ śoṇitābhyukṣitāṅgasya rudrasyevorjitaṃ mahat
english: As he took the lives of these, the form of Ādhirathi, his limbs drenched with blood, grew vast and mighty, like that of Rudra himself.

sanskrit: tatra bhārata karṇena mātaṅgās tāḍitāḥ śaraiḥ sarvato 'bhyadravan bhītāḥ kurvanto mahad ākulam
english: There, O Bhārata, the elephants struck by Karṇa's arrows, panic-stricken, fled in all directions, spreading great confusion.

sanskrit: nipetur urvyāṃ samare karṇasāyakapīḍitāḥ kurvanto vividhān nādān vajranunnā ivācalāḥ
english: Tormented by Karṇa's shafts, they fell to the earth in the battle, uttering manifold cries, like mountains shattered by the thunderbolt.

sanskrit: gajavājimanuṣyaiś ca nipatadbhiḥ samantataḥ rathaiś cāvagatair mārge paryastīryata medinī
english: With elephants, horses, and men falling on every side, and with chariots overturned upon the road, the earth was strewn over.

sanskrit: naiva bhīṣmo na ca droṇo nāpy anye yudhi tāvakāḥ cakruḥ sma tādṛśaṃ karma yādṛśaṃ vai kṛtaṃ raṇe
english: Neither Bhīṣma nor Droṇa, nor any other of your men in war, performed such a deed as was done in that battle.

sanskrit: sūtaputreṇa nāgeṣu ratheṣu ca hayeṣu ca nareṣu ca naravyāghra kṛtaṃ sma kadanaṃ mahat
english: By the son of the sūta, O tiger among men, a great slaughter was wrought among elephants, chariots, horses, and men.

sanskrit: mṛgamadhye yathā siṃho dṛśyate nirbhayaś caran pāñcālānāṃ tathā madhye karṇo 'carad abhītavat
english: As a lion is seen ranging fearlessly amid the deer, so Karṇa moved without fear amid the Pāñcālas.

sanskrit: yathā mṛgagaṇāṃs trastān siṃho drāvayate diśaḥ pāñcālānāṃ rathavrātān karṇo drāvayate tathā
english: As a lion drives the terrified herds of deer to the four quarters, so Karṇa drove the throngs of Pāñcāla chariots.

sanskrit: siṃhāsyaṃ ca yathā prāpya na jīvanti mṛgāḥ kva cit tathā karṇam anuprāpya na jīvanti mahārathāḥ
english: As deer that come within the jaws of a lion can nowhere survive, so the great chariot-warriors who came upon Karṇa did not live.

sanskrit: vaiśvānaraṃ yathā dīptaṃ dahyante prāpya vai janāḥ karṇāgninā raṇe tadvad dagdhā bhārata sṛñjayāḥ
english: As men are consumed when they come upon a blazing fire, so, O Bhārata, the Sṛñjayas were burned in battle by the fire that was Karṇa.

sanskrit: karṇena cediṣv ekena pāñcāleṣu ca bhārata viśrāvya nāma nihatā bahavaḥ śūrasaṃmatāḥ
english: By Karṇa alone, O Bhārata, among the Cedis and the Pāñcālas, many esteemed as heroes were slain, each named aloud as he fell.

sanskrit: mama cāsīn manuṣyendra dṛṣṭvā karṇasya vikramam naiko 'py ādhirather jīvan pāñcālyo mokṣyate yudhi
english: And to me, O lord of men, beholding Karṇa's prowess, it seemed that not a single Pāñcāla would escape alive from Ādhirathi in the battle.

sanskrit: pāñcālān vidhaman saṃkhye sūtaputraḥ pratāpavān abhyadhāvata saṃkruddho dharmaputraṃ yudhiṣṭhiram
english: Scattering the Pāñcālas in the fight, the valiant son of the sūta, in fury, rushed against Yudhiṣṭhira, the son of Dharma.

sanskrit: dhṛṣṭadyumnaś ca rājānaṃ draupadeyāś ca māriṣa parivavrur amitraghnaṃ śataśaś cāpare janāḥ
english: Then Dhṛṣṭadyumna and the sons of Draupadī, O venerable one, and hundreds of other men surrounded that slayer of foes to protect the king.

sanskrit: śikhaṇḍī sahadevaś ca nakulo nākulis tathā janamejayaḥ śiner naptā bahavaś ca prabhadrakāḥ
english: Śikhaṇḍin and Sahadeva, Nakula and the son of Nakula, Janamejaya, the grandson of Śini, and many of the Prabhadrakas—

sanskrit: ete purogamā bhūtvā dhṛṣṭadyumnasya saṃyuge karṇam asyantaṃ iṣvastrair vicerur amitaujasaḥ
english: these, of boundless might, becoming the vanguard of Dhṛṣṭadyumna in the conflict, ranged against Karṇa as he loosed his missiles and arrows.

sanskrit: tāṃs tatrādhirathiḥ saṃkhye cedipāñcālapāṇḍavān eko bahūn abhyapatad garutman pannagān iva
english: There in the fight Ādhirathi, alone, fell upon those many—Cedis, Pāñcālas, and Pāṇḍavas—as Garuḍa swoops upon serpents.

sanskrit: bhīmasenas tu saṃkruddhaḥ kurūn madrān sakekayān ekaḥ saṃkhye maheṣvāso yodhayan bahv aśobhata
english: Bhīmasena, that mighty archer, enraged, battling alone in the fight against the Kurus, the Madras, and the Kekayas, shone resplendent.

sanskrit: tatra marmasu bhīmena nārācais tāḍitā gajāḥ prapatanto hatārohāḥ kampayanti sma medinīm
english: There elephants struck by Bhīma's iron shafts in their vital parts, their riders slain, fell down and made the earth tremble.

sanskrit: vājinaś ca hatārohāḥ pattayaś ca gatāsavaḥ śerate yudhi nirbhinnā vamanto rudhiraṃ bahu
english: Horses with their riders slain, and foot-soldiers bereft of life, lay pierced upon the field, vomiting blood in streams.

sanskrit: sahasraśaś ca rathinaḥ patitāḥ patitāyudhāḥ akṣatāḥ samadṛśyanta bhīmād bhītā gatāsavaḥ
english: And chariot-warriors by the thousand, fallen with their weapons fallen from their hands, were seen lifeless—unwounded, slain by very terror of Bhīma.

sanskrit: rathibhir vājibhiḥ sūtaiḥ pattibhiś ca tathā gajaiḥ bhīmasenaśaracchinnair āstīrṇā vasudhābhavat
english: With chariot-warriors, horses, charioteers, foot-soldiers, and elephants, all hewn apart by Bhīmasena's arrows, the earth was strewn over.

sanskrit: tat stambhitam ivātiṣṭhad bhīmasenabalārditam duryodhanabalaṃ rājan nirutsāhaṃ kṛtavraṇam
english: Tormented by Bhīmasena's might, the host of Duryodhana, O king, stood as though paralyzed—spiritless and grievously wounded.

sanskrit: niśceṣṭaṃ tumule dīnaṃ babhau tasmin mahāraṇe prasannasalilaḥ kāle yathā syāt sāgaro nṛpa
english: Motionless and wretched in that great and tumultuous battle, it appeared, O king, like the ocean grown still with calm waters in its season.

sanskrit: manyuvīryabalopetaṃ balāt paryavaropitam abhavat tava putrasya tat sainyam iṣubhis tadā rudhiraughapariklinnaṃ rudhirārdraṃ babhūva ha
english: That army of your son, endowed with wrath, valor, and strength, was then forcibly beaten down by arrows, and soaked in floods of blood, it grew drenched and dripping with gore.

sanskrit: sūtaputro raṇe kruddhaḥ pāṇḍavānām anīkinīm bhīmasenaḥ kurūṃś cāpi drāvayan bahv aśobhata
english: The son of the sūta, enraged in battle, driving back the host of the Pāṇḍavas, and Bhīmasena driving back the Kurus, each shone in surpassing splendor.

sanskrit: vartamāne tathā raudre saṃgrāme 'dbhutadarśane nihatya pṛtanāmadhye saṃśaptakagaṇān bahūn
english: As that fierce and wondrous battle went on, Arjuna, having slain in the midst of the host the many bands of the Saṃśaptakas—

sanskrit: arjuno jayatāṃ śreṣṭho vāsudevam athābravīt prabhagnaṃ balam etad dhi yotsyamānaṃ janārdana
english: —Arjuna, foremost of the victorious, then said to Vāsudeva: "This host that would fight on is broken, O Janārdana.

sanskrit: ete dhāvanti sagaṇāḥ saṃśaptakamahārathāḥ apārayanto madbāṇān siṃhaśabdān mṛgā iva
english: These great Saṃśaptaka chariot-warriors flee with all their bands, unable to withstand my arrows, as deer flee the lion's roar.

sanskrit: dīryate ca mahat sainyaṃ sṛñjayānāṃ mahāraṇe hastikakṣyo hy asau kṛṣṇa ketuḥ karṇasya dhīmataḥ dṛśyate rājasainyasya madhye vicarato muhuḥ
english: And the great host of the Sṛñjayas is being rent apart in this great battle, O Kṛṣṇa; yonder elephant-girth banner of the wise Karṇa is seen ranging again and again amid the royal army.

sanskrit: na ca karṇaṃ raṇe śaktā jetum anye mahārathāḥ jānīte hi bhavān karṇaṃ vīryavantaṃ parākrame
english: The other great chariot-warriors are not able to vanquish Karṇa in battle; for you know Karṇa to be a man of valor in prowess.

sanskrit: tatra yāhi yataḥ karṇo drāvayaty eṣa no balam
english: Drive there, then, to where Karṇa is putting our host to flight.

sanskrit: varjayitvā raṇe yāhi sūtaputraṃ mahāratham śramo mā bādhate kṛṣṇa yathā vā tava rocate
english: Or, avoiding the great chariot-warrior, the son of the sūta, drive on through the battle, that weariness may not oppress you, O Kṛṣṇa—or as it pleases you."

sanskrit: etac chrutvā mahārāja govindaḥ prahasann iva abravīd arjunaṃ tūrṇaṃ kauravāñ jahi pāṇḍava
english: Hearing this, O great king, Govinda, as if smiling, said to Arjuna at once: "Swiftly slay the Kauravas, O son of Pāṇḍu."

sanskrit: tatas tava mahat sainyaṃ govindapreritā hayāḥ haṃsavarṇāḥ praviviśur vahantaḥ kṛṣṇapāṇḍavau
english: Then the swan-white horses, urged on by Govinda, bearing Kṛṣṇa and the son of Pāṇḍu, entered into that great host of yours.

sanskrit: keśavaprahitair aśvaiḥ śvetaiḥ kāñcanabhūṣaṇaiḥ praviśadbhis tava balaṃ caturdiśam abhidyata
english: As the white horses adorned with gold, driven by Keśava, entered your army, it was rent asunder on all four sides.

sanskrit: tau vidārya mahāsenāṃ praviṣṭau keśavārjunau kruddhau saṃrambharaktākṣau vyabhrājetāṃ mahādyutī
english: Cleaving the great army and entering within, Keśava and Arjuna, enraged, their eyes red with fury, shone forth in mighty splendor.

sanskrit: yuddhaśauṇḍau samāhūtāv aribhis tau raṇādhvaram yajvabhir vidhināhūtau makhe devāv ivāśvinau
english: Those two, eager for battle, summoned by their foes to the sacrifice of war, shone like the two Aśvin gods duly invoked by sacrificers at the rite.

sanskrit: kruddhau tau tu naravyāghrau vegavantau babhūvatuḥ talaśabdena ruṣitau yathā nāgau mahāhave
english: Those two tigers among men, enraged, grew swift and impetuous, like two elephants goaded to fury by the slap of hands in the great battle.

sanskrit: vigāhan sa rathānīkam aśvasaṃghāṃś ca phalgunaḥ vyacarat pṛtanāmadhye pāśahasta ivāntakaḥ
english: Plunging into the array of chariots and the squadrons of horse, Phalguna ranged through the midst of the host like Death with noose in hand.

sanskrit: taṃ dṛṣṭvā yudhi vikrāntaṃ senāyāṃ tava bhārata saṃśaptakagaṇān bhūyaḥ putras te samacodayat
english: Seeing him advancing valiantly within your army in the fight, O Bhārata, your son once more urged on the bands of the Saṃśaptakas.

sanskrit: tato rathasahasreṇa dviradānāṃ tribhiḥ śataiḥ caturdaśasahasraiś ca turagāṇāṃ mahāhave
english: Then with a thousand chariots, three hundred elephants, and fourteen thousand horse in that great battle—

sanskrit: dvābhyāṃ śatasahasrābhyāṃ padātīnāṃ ca dhanvinām śūrāṇāṃ nāmalabdhānāṃ viditānāṃ samantataḥ abhyavartanta tau vīrau chādayanto mahārathāḥ
english: —and with two hundred thousand foot-soldiers and archers, heroes who had won renown and were known on every side, those great chariot-warriors advanced against the two heroes, overwhelming them.

sanskrit: sa chādyamānaḥ samare śaraiḥ parabalārdanaḥ darśayan raudram ātmānaṃ pāśahasta ivāntakaḥ nighnan saṃśaptakān pārthaḥ prekṣaṇīyataro 'bhavat
english: Though covered over with arrows in the battle, that crusher of hostile hosts, the son of Pṛthā, revealing his terrible self like Death with noose in hand and slaying the Saṃśaptakas, became all the more a sight to behold.

sanskrit: tato vidyutprabhair bāṇaiḥ kārtasvaravibhūṣitaiḥ nirantaram ivākāśam āsīn nunnaiḥ kirīṭinā
english: Then, with arrows bright as lightning and adorned with gold, sped by the Diademed One, the very sky seemed without an interval between them.

sanskrit: kirīṭibhujanirmuktaiḥ saṃpatadbhir mahāśaraiḥ samācchannaṃ babhau sarvaṃ kādraveyair iva prabho
english: With the great arrows loosed from the arm of the Diademed One falling thick, all things appeared overspread, O lord, as if by the brood of Kadrū.

sanskrit: rukmapuṅkhān prasannāgrāñ śarān saṃnataparvaṇaḥ adarśayad ameyātmā dikṣu sarvāsu pāṇḍavaḥ
english: Arrows golden-shafted, bright-pointed, and smooth-jointed, the Pāṇḍava of measureless soul displayed in all directions.

sanskrit: hatvā daśa sahasrāṇi pārthivānāṃ mahārathaḥ saṃśaptakānāṃ kaunteyaḥ prapakṣaṃ tvarito 'bhyayāt
english: Having slain ten thousand of the Saṃśaptaka kings, the great chariot-warrior, the son of Kuntī, hastened against their flanking force.

sanskrit: prapakṣaṃ sa samāsādya pārthaḥ kāmbojarakṣitam pramamātha balād bāṇair dānavān iva vāsavaḥ
english: Reaching that flanking force, guarded by the Kāmbojas, the son of Pṛthā crushed it by force with his arrows, as Vāsava crushed the Dānavas.

sanskrit: pracicchedāśu bhallaiś ca dviṣatām ātatāyinām śastrapāṇīṃs tathā bāhūṃs tathāpi ca śirāṃsy uta
english: With his broad-headed shafts he swiftly cut away the weapon-grasping hands of the assailing foes, and their arms, and likewise their heads.

sanskrit: aṅgāṅgāvayavaiś chinnair vyāyudhās te 'patan kṣitau viṣvagvātābhisaṃbhagnā bahuśākhā iva drumāḥ
english: With their limbs and members severed, weaponless, they fell to the earth, like many-branched trees shattered by a wind blowing on every side.

sanskrit: hastyaśvarathapattīnāṃ vrātān nighnantam arjunam sudakṣiṇād avarajaḥ śaravṛṣṭyābhyavīvṛṣat
english: Upon Arjuna, as he slew the throngs of elephants, horses, chariots, and foot, the younger brother of Sudakṣiṇa rained down a shower of arrows.

sanskrit: asyāsyato 'rdhacandrābhyāṃ sa bāhū parighopamau pūrṇacandrābhavaktraṃ ca kṣureṇābhyahanac chiraḥ
english: As he shot, Arjuna struck off with two crescent-headed arrows his two arms, like iron bludgeons, and with a razor-edged shaft his head, whose face was bright as the full moon.

sanskrit: sa papāta tato vāhāt svalohitaparisravaḥ manaḥśilāgireḥ śṛṅgaṃ vajreṇevāvadāritam
english: He fell then from his mount, streaming with his own blood, like a peak of a realgar-red mountain riven by the thunderbolt.

sanskrit: sudakṣiṇād avarajaṃ kāmbojaṃ dadṛśur hatam prāṃśuṃ kamalapatrākṣam atyarthaṃ priyadarśanam kāñcanastambhasaṃkāśaṃ bhinnaṃ hemagiriṃ yathā
english: They beheld the younger brother of Sudakṣiṇa, the Kāmboja, slain—tall, his eyes like lotus-petals, exceedingly fair to look upon, resembling a pillar of gold, like a golden mountain cleft asunder.

sanskrit: tato 'bhavat punar yuddhaṃ ghoram adbhutadarśanam nānāvasthāś ca yodhānāṃ babhūvus tatra yudhyatām
english: Then once more the battle grew terrible and wondrous to behold, and many were the conditions of the warriors fighting there.

sanskrit: eteṣv āvarjitair aśvaiḥ kāmbojair yavanaiḥ śakaiḥ śoṇitāktais tadā raktaṃ sarvam āsīd viśāṃ pate
english: With the horses of these Kāmbojas, Yavanas, and Śakas struck down and smeared with blood, all then became red, O lord of peoples.

sanskrit: rathai rathāśvasūtaiś ca hatārohaiś ca vājibhiḥ dviradaiś ca hatārohair mahāmātrair hatadvipaiḥ anyonyena mahārāja kṛto ghoro janakṣayaḥ
english: By chariots, by chariot-horses and charioteers, by horses with their riders slain, by elephants with their riders slain, and by mahouts whose elephants were slain, O great king, a fearful destruction of men was wrought upon one another.

sanskrit: tasmin prapakṣe pakṣe ca vadhyamāne mahātmanā arjunaṃ jayatāṃ śreṣṭhaṃ tvarito drauṇir āyayau
english: As that flanking force and the wing were being slain by the great-souled one, the son of Droṇa hastened against Arjuna, foremost of the victorious.

sanskrit: vidhunvāno mahac cāpaṃ kārtasvaravibhūṣitam ādadānaḥ śarān ghorān svaraśmīn iva bhāskaraḥ
english: Brandishing his great bow adorned with gold, and taking up his terrible arrows like the sun gathering its own rays.

sanskrit: taiḥ patadbhir mahārāja drauṇimuktaiḥ samantataḥ saṃchāditau rathasthau tāv ubhau kṛṣṇadhanaṃjayau
english: By those arrows loosed by the son of Droṇa, falling on every side, O great king, the two—Kṛṣṇa and Dhanaṃjaya—standing in their chariot, were covered over.

sanskrit: tataḥ śaraśatais tīkṣṇair bhāradvājaḥ pratāpavān niśceṣṭau tāv ubhau cakre yuddhe mādhavapāṇḍavau
english: Then with hundreds of sharp arrows the valiant son of Bhāradvāja rendered both Mādhava and the son of Pāṇḍu motionless in the battle.

sanskrit: hāhākṛtam abhūt sarvaṃ jaṅgamaṃ sthāvaraṃ tathā carācarasya goptārau dṛṣṭvā saṃchāditau śaraiḥ
english: All things, moving and unmoving, broke into cries of woe, seeing the two protectors of all that moves and is still covered over with arrows.

sanskrit: siddhacāraṇasaṃghāś ca saṃpetur vai samantataḥ cintayanto bhaved adya lokānāṃ svasty apīty aha
english: And the hosts of Siddhas and Cāraṇas gathered together from every side, anxiously wondering whether the welfare of the worlds might yet be preserved this day.

sanskrit: na mayā tādṛśo rājan dṛṣṭapūrvaḥ parākramaḥ saṃjajñe yādṛśo drauṇeḥ kṛṣṇau saṃchādayiṣyataḥ
english: Never before, O king, had I beheld such prowess as arose in the son of Droṇa as he covered the two Kṛṣṇas over with arrows.

sanskrit: drauṇes tu dhanuṣaḥ śabdam ahitatrāsanaṃ raṇe aśrauṣaṃ bahuśo rājan siṃhasya nadato yathā
english: The twang of the son of Droṇa's bow, terrifying his foes in the battle, I heard again and again, O king, like the roaring of a lion.

sanskrit: jyā cāsya carato yuddhe savyadakṣiṇam asyataḥ vidyud ambudamadhyasthā bhrājamāneva sābhavat
english: And his bowstring, as he ranged through the battle shooting to left and right, became like lightning flashing in the midst of the clouds.

sanskrit: sa tathā kṣiprakārī ca dṛḍhahastaś ca pāṇḍavaḥ saṃmohaṃ paramaṃ gatvā praikṣata droṇajaṃ tataḥ
english: Then the Pāṇḍava, swift of action and firm of hand though he was, fell into utter bewilderment and gazed upon the son of Droṇa.

sanskrit: sa vikramaṃ hṛtaṃ mene ātmanaḥ sumahātmanā tathāsya samare rājan vapur āsīt sudurdṛśam
english: He deemed his own prowess robbed from him by that exceedingly great-souled one; and his form in the battle, O king, became hard to look upon.

sanskrit: drauṇipāṇḍavayor evaṃ vartamāne mahāraṇe vardhamāne ca rājendra droṇaputre mahābale hīyamāne ca kaunteye kṛṣṇaṃ roṣaḥ samabhyayāt
english: As the great battle between the son of Droṇa and the Pāṇḍava went on thus, O lord of kings, with the mighty son of Droṇa waxing strong and the son of Kuntī failing, wrath came upon Kṛṣṇa.

sanskrit: sa roṣān niḥśvasan rājan nirdahann iva cakṣuṣā drauṇiṃ hy apaśyat saṃgrāme phalgunaṃ ca muhur muhuḥ
english: Sighing in his anger, O king, and seeming to burn with his very eyes, he looked again and again upon the son of Droṇa and upon Phalguna in the battle.

sanskrit: tataḥ kruddho 'bravīt kṛṣṇaḥ pārthaṃ sapraṇayaṃ tadā atyadbhutam idaṃ pārtha tava paśyāmi saṃyuge atiśete hi yatra tvā droṇaputro 'dya bhārata
english: Then in his wrath Kṛṣṇa spoke to the son of Pṛthā with affection: "Most wondrous is this I see of you in battle, O Pārtha—that the son of Droṇa surpasses you this day, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: kaccit te gāṇḍivaṃ haste rathe tiṣṭhasi cārjuna kaccit kuśalinau bāhū kaccid vīryaṃ tad eva te
english: Is the Gāṇḍīva yet in your hand, and do you stand upon your chariot, O Arjuna? Are your two arms unharmed? Is your valor still the same as ever?"

sanskrit: evam uktas tu kṛṣṇena kṣiptvā bhallāṃś caturdaśa tvaramāṇas tvarākāle drauṇer dhanur athācchinat dhvajaṃ chatraṃ patākāṃ ca rathaṃ śaktiṃ gadāṃ tathā
english: Thus addressed by Kṛṣṇa, Arjuna, hastening in that hour for haste, loosed fourteen broad-headed shafts and cut asunder the bow of the son of Droṇa, and his standard, parasol, and banner, his chariot, his lance, and his mace.

sanskrit: jatrudeśe ca subhṛśaṃ vatsadantair atāḍayat sa mūrcchāṃ paramāṃ gatvā dhvajayaṣṭiṃ samāśritaḥ
english: And he smote him hard upon the collarbone with calf-tooth arrows; and the son of Droṇa, falling into a deep swoon, sank down clinging to his banner-staff.
